punchline: A little girl in a Texas well in 1987 drew the world's attention, while larger crises affecting many more people drew less.
thirty_sec: Paul Bloom points to a 1987 case in Midland, Texas, where a little girl was stuck in a well and many people cared about her, while crises that affected far more people drew less of that attention. He doesn't tell us to stop caring. He asks for rational compassion: let feeling start the impulse to help, then ask what does the most good, as effective altruists do.
